name: vwap_ema_5m
hypothesis: 5-minute VWAP + 9/21 EMA crossover entries, skipping 11:30-13:30 ET, ATR stop, flat by 15:50
why: no edge on 60 days of 5-minute data: trade t-stats below 1 on NVDA, SPY and QQQ
do_not_repeat: plain VWAP/EMA crossover entries on 5-minute bars

name: vwap_ema_trend_day
hypothesis: the VWAP/EMA strategy only on trend days, when the day opens beyond the prior day's high or low
why: the trend-day filter cut trades but did not create an edge (t-stat below 1)

name: vwap_ema_time_exit
hypothesis: the VWAP/EMA strategy with a fixed time-based exit instead of a trailing stop
why: changing the exit did not change the result: no edge
do_not_repeat: swapping exits to rescue an entry with no edge

name: opening_range_breakout
hypothesis: trade the first close beyond the 15-minute (5m bars) or 60-minute (1h bars) opening range, stop at the other side
why: 2-year hourly test made money in the first half and lost it in the second: unstable, consistent with noise
do_not_repeat: opening-range breakouts on large-cap US stocks and ETFs

name: tradingagents_free_model
hypothesis: the TradingAgents multi-agent pipeline on Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite picks the direction of the next 5 trading days
why: 27 of 57 directional calls right (47%); stated ~62% confidence every week, Brier score worse than always saying 50%
do_not_repeat: judging the agent pipeline on a weak free model; retest only with a stronger model

name: harry_sharp_bias
hypothesis: when the prior daily candle and the pre-New York 4-hour candle close the same way, the New York session follows
why: right 47.7% to 52.6% of the time over 549 days vs about 50% by chance; no version significant
do_not_repeat: direction-of-prior-candles bias rules on index futures

name: harry_sharp_entry
symbol: NQ, ES, YM, RTY, GC futures
hypothesis: range, strong breakout close, then a dip-and-reclaim entry at 1:1 risk to reward wins 70% of the time
why: won 47% to 57% on 60 days (break-even about 53% after costs); largest sample's likely range 48-62%, below the 70% claim
do_not_repeat: mechanical versions of range-breakout-with-pullback entries at 1:1

name: spy_sma200_trend
hypothesis: holding SPY only above its 200-day moving average avoids big bear markets and gives a better return for the risk than always holding
disproof: Sharpe on the test years not above buy-and-hold, or too few trades to judge
why: test: only 18 trades (needs 30); test: Sharpe 0.63 does not beat buy-and-hold 0.68; test: trade t-stat 1.18 is below the 2.50 required
